transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-05-21
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (Head of ML - Lumenion), Marcus Reed (Platform), Anika Bose (CISO), Tom Hsu (Data Eng), Jordan Lee (Product)

Auto-generated Summary:
- Goal: Scope POC deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private) for Lumenion's inference workload; agree success criteria, benchmark plan, and pilot timeline.
- Main constraints: P95 latency target, cost envelope, data residency / compliance (KMS/HSM, audit logs), and predictable throughput for peak batch jobs.
- Agreed next steps: Redwood to send pricing & SOW, Diego to propose benchmark plan, Lumenion to share sample prompts and traffic histogram, schedule benchmark week.

Topics Covered:
- production success criteria, latency/throughput targets, cost per 1k tokens, warm vs cold start behavior
- hosting tradeoffs: host vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem)
- benchmarking approach: synthetic vs replay, dataset size, metrics to capture
- security: SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS/HSM, SOC2 evidence
- timelines and pilot gating

Questions (raised during call):
- What does Redwood's dedicated burst policy look like?
- How do we measure regressed quality vs baseline?
- Can private deployment meet our data residency constraints within 8 weeks?

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, I'm Maya, AE, and with me is Diego our solutions engineer.
[00:09] Sofia (Lumenion): Hi, Sofia here. we're trying to figure out which hosting path makes sense for our inference POC. we have some latency-sensitive ops and also batch summarization jobs.
[00:18] Diego (Redwood SE): cool. maybe start with current stack? what are you running now for inference?
[00:22] Marcus (Lumenion): we're on a mix — in-house GPU nodes for heavy batches, and some CPU-based microservices for light requests. no unified inference layer yet.
[00:30] Jordan (Product): goal is to ship a feature in Q3 that does real-time response to customer queries, so sub-200ms p95 ideal, but cost matters.
[00:39] Anika (CISO): for us security is a blocker: keys must be customer-managed in KMS, audit logs retained 2 years, and we need SOC2 evidence.
[00:47] Maya: great, that's helpful. so on success criteria we usually split into performance, quality, cost, and security. Diego, maybe run through hosting tradeoffs quickly?
[00:56] Diego: yeah. short version — Hosted is fastest to get started: Redwood API, no infra to manage, predictable unit pricing. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale, but takes lead time to provision. Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you control for keys and network isolation but is longer to stand up and needs more ops on your side.
[01:18] Tom (Data Eng): can you quantify lead times? like if we pick dedicated how long to spin up capacity?
[01:23] Maya: typical lead time for dedicated is 2–4 weeks after contract; private on-prem can be 6–10 weeks depending on procurement and networking. hosted is immediate — we can issue keys and start in a day.
[01:34] Sofia: ok. our non-negotiable: p95 <= 150ms for single-turn, throughput 200 qps during peak, and batch jobs that can be scheduled overnight. cost target: less than $0.50 per 1k tokens equivalent.
[01:48] Diego: good concrete numbers. couple clarifications — is the 200 qps sustained or burst?
[01:52] Sofia: burst for 10 minutes at peak, sustained average is more like 50 qps.
[01:57] Diego: perfect. that changes batching strategy, we can do small micro-batches for low-latency and larger batch window for overnight jobs.
[02:06] Marcus: can Redwood Dedicated guarantee the p95? what's the SLA?
[02:10] Maya: our Dedicated offering has SLA-backed latency and uptime targets; practically we design for p95 targets via reserved pools and autoscaling policies. for benchs we recommend testing both hosted and a dedicated pilot so you can see variance.
[02:22] Anika: and how about KMS/HSM? our security team won't accept vendor-managed keys.
[02:27] Diego: we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS on hosted and dedicated, and for private we can integrate with your HSM or KMS. there are some additional config steps and audits for private.
[02:38] Jordan: what about model quantization and quality drop? we use a custom LLM fine-tuned, if you quantize for cost we can't lose >2% accuracy on our eval set.
[02:49] Diego: we usually provide quantization recommendations per model. part of the benchmark is to run eval prompts pre/post quantization and compute regression metrics. we can set an automated regression alert if quality drops beyond agreed thresholds.
[03:03] Sofia: benchmarking plan? we want a realistic replay of production traffic not just synthetic.
[03:08] Diego: agreed. propose: you share 2k representative prompts + traffic histogram (latency and token distribution). Redwood will run three test passes: hosted baseline, dedicated baseline (if provisioned), and private if you want to bring it up. each pass: 100k tokens total, measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, error rate, and cost per 1k tokens.
[03:29] Marcus: is 100k tokens enough? our monthly is ~150M tokens.
[03:33] Diego: for perf characteristics 100k with representative distribution is enough to estimate latency and burst behavior. for cost extrapolation we'll scale linearly but note model sequence length variance matters.
[03:44] Tom: replay fidelity — do you capture KV cache warm states? cold start vs warm affects latency a lot.
[03:49] Diego: yep, good point. we'll run cold-start and warmed runs, measure KV cache hit rates. we'll also exercise prefix caching scenarios.
[03:57] Maya: on timelines — if we start next week, Diego can provision a hosted bench immediately; dedicated pilot provisioning depends on contract approval but we can aim to have dedicated nodes in 2–3 weeks. private on-prem likely longer.
[04:10] Anika: our procurement timeline is tight. if hosted meets our security bar with customer-managed KMS and SOC2 artifacts would we consider hosted for production?
[04:18] Maya: it's possible. hosted with VPC peering and customer KMS can satisfy many controls. the gating question will be audit log retention and contractual SLAs; Diego will annotate the security packet with exact controls.
[04:28] Diego: I'll attach the SOC2 evidence, KMS integration guide, and RBAC/SSO doc. note: SAML SSO is supported and we have token-level audit logs with configurable retention.
[04:39] Jordan: we need a success rubric for the POC. suggested: 1) Performance: p95 <=150ms on 90% of test windows, 2) Quality: regression <=2% on eval set, 3) Cost: projected cost within the $0.50/1k tokens envelope, 4) Ops: deployment repeatable and meets security checklist.
[04:57] Sofia: agree. also add a reliability check: no more than 1% error rate during peak test.
[05:02] Diego: added. we'll propose a pass/fail threshold and a scorecard so it's objective.
[05:07] Tom: what's the benchmark environment footprint? how many GPUs for dedicated tests?
[05:12] Diego: for your throughput target (200 qps burst) baseline we'd recommend 4x A100-equivalent GPUs for deterministic low-latency. dedicated pools can be tuned, and we recommend testing both quantized bfloat16 and int8 variants.
[05:27] Marcus: cost-wise is dedicated cheaper at that scale?
[05:30] Maya: often yes — dedicated reserved capacity and higher utilization drive unit cost down. we'll put a modeled cost comparison in the pricing doc.
[05:36] Jordan: are there any gotchas on routing/fallbacks? we want graceful degradation if capacity is maxed.
[05:41] Diego: Redwood supports smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants or lower-cost tiers. you can set policies like prefer low-latency region then fallback to lower-cost model if required.
[05:52] Anika: logging and audit — can we push logs into our SIEM?
[05:55] Diego: yes, audit logs can be exported to your S3 or pushed to SIEM via our connectors; retention configurable.
[06:03] Maya: next steps recap — we'll send pricing and pilot SOW, Diego will send benchmark plan and security docs, you (Sofia) will share prompts and traffic histogram. aim to run bench week of 2026-05-27 and meet 2026-05-28 to review. sound right?
[06:19] Sofia: yes. @Anika we'll review the security packet and if hosted meets controls we can fast-track.
[06:25] Anika: noted. one concern — latency SLO in contract; procurement will need specific penalties.
[06:30] Maya: we can include SLA language in SOW for dedicated; hosted has standard T&Cs we can escalate.
[06:36] Tom: small nit — during benchmarks please include sequence length buckets, we have a long-tail of long prompts.
[06:41] Diego: will do, sequence length buckets & KV cache hit analysis.
[06:44] Jordan: I also want to see an end-to-end template for production rollout — can you share a prod checklist?
[06:49] Maya: yes, we'll include a prod rollout checklist with canary steps, metrics to monitor, and fallback policies.
[06:56] Sofia: good. any blockers left?
[06:58] Marcus: none from infra aside from contract timelines.
[07:02] Maya: ok we'll wrap. thanks everyone.

End of meeting.
